flags.quote: The position stays even, but moving your pawn to f4 puts it at risk of attack from the black pawn. A better move would have been moving your g1-knight to f3.
flags.critique: That is the King's Gambit, not a hanging-pawn accident. I offered the f-pawn on purpose to open the f-file and unbalance the king, and you told me I left a pawn en prise. If Nf3 is safer, say it develops and covers h4 — do not teach 'don't hang the f-pawn' for a famous pawn sacrifice.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e5 with your f-pawn puts it at risk of attack from the black c6-knight. A better move would have been moving your g1-knight to f3 because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: This is the Qh4+ trap, the whole reason 3.fxe5 is a 567-centipawn blunder, and you talked about the e-pawn hanging to a knight. Nf3 is better because it covers h4, not because I can 'likely take a pawn.' You lectured pawn structure-adjacent hanging while the queen check wins the rook or the king walk.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to c5 is a blunder, but moving your queen to h4 would be better because you pin the pawn to the rook and then fork the white king and the white h1-rook.
flags.critique: Qh4+ is check. The idea is Ke2 or g3, and after g3 then Qxe4+ forks king and rook — not a pin of some unnamed pawn to a rook. You had the right suggestion and still described the wrong tactic, and you never said the word check. Reasons on the played move are just 'development,' which is how you hide a 593-centipawn miss.

flags.quote: Moving your g1-knight to f3 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: Two plies ago you should have been screaming Qh4+. Nf3 is the cover of h4 — that is the lesson. 'Saves your pawn from capture' is a side effect of defending e5. I just survived a famous queen check and you told me I was pawn-sitting.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d6 is a mistake, but taking the pawn on e5 with your c6-knight would be better because you can likely pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: Nxe5 takes a hanging pawn. If White recaptures Nxe5, Qh4+ comes back. There is no 'likely pin the pawn to the rook' on the capture itself. Empty reasons, invented tactic, missed the same queen check for a third time.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d4 is a blunder, but taking the pawn on d6 with your e-pawn would be better.
flags.critique: Better how? exd6 takes the pawn that is attacking e5 and opens the file; d4 leaves e5 hanging and invites dxe5. A blunder with no because-clause is just a verdict. Reasons even say saves_piece and king_safer, which is not why this dumpstered the eval.

flags.quote: Moving your c5-bishop to b6 is a blunder, but taking the pawn on d4 with your c6-knight would be better because you can likely pin the knight to the queen.
flags.critique: Nxd4 is about the d-pawn and, if Nxd4 Nxd4, Qh4+ again because the knight left f3. 'Likely pin the knight to the queen' is a PV ghost. Stop selling me pins that are not on the board.

flags.quote: Moving your c8-bishop to d7 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: You just praised Bb5 for pinning my knight to the king. Bd7 is the unpin. 'Strongest move' plus development is a shrug. Teach the pin break.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to a6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: No reason at all. a6 asks the bishop on b5 whether it takes or leaves. If you cannot say that, do not call it strongest and walk away.

flags.quote: Moving your b5-bishop to c4 is the strongest move because it saves your c4-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: I moved the bishop TO c4, then you told me that saved the c4-bishop. a6 was attacking it on b5; I retreated. Name the attacked piece on the square it left, not the square it fled to.

flags.quote: Moving your g8-knight to e7 is a blunder, but taking the pawn on e5 with your d-pawn would be better.
flags.critique: dxe5 finally takes the extra e-pawn that has been sitting on my chest since move 3. You did not say I win a pawn, I open the d-file, or that Nge7 leaves that pawn alive. Blunder with a nameless 'better.'

flags.quote: You are still winning, but taking the pawn on f7 with your c4-bishop puts it where the black king can take and you lose a knight. A better move would have been taking the pawn on d6 with your e-pawn.
flags.critique: The king takes a bishop. I did not lose a knight; I sacrificed a bishop for a pawn and an exposed king. SEE rounded the loss to 'a knight' and you printed it like a fact. I cannot trust material copy after that.

flags.quote: Moving your f3-knight to g5 leaves your pawn hanging to the black c6-knight and pawn. A better move would have been moving your pawn to e6 because you fork the black d7-bishop and the black king.
flags.critique: The e6+ fork is the real lesson and you almost taught it. Then you led with 'your pawn' hanging to a knight and a pawn — which pawn? d4? e5? If the headline is a missed king-and-bishop fork, lead with that, not an unnamed hanging pawn.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e6 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: Last move you wanted e6+ as a fork. Now the same push is 'saves your pawn,' while you even detected a passed pawn and ignored it. e6 is a wedge on d7/f7, not a panic retreat. Pick one story.

flags.quote: Moving your d7-bishop to e8 is the strongest move because it saves your e8-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: Same gag as Bc4. I ran the bishop off d7 so e6 would not eat it, and you called it saving the e8-bishop. I already know where it landed. Tell me it steps off the fork square.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your queen to f3 leaves your pawn hanging to the black b6-bishop and c6-knight. A better move would have been moving your g5-knight to f7 because you fork the black queen and the black h8-rook.
flags.critique: Nf7 forking queen and rook is the right suggestion. d4 is not hanging — Nc3 still guards it. Two attackers versus one defender is a pawn I can win, not a free piece. Do not say hanging when it is just underdefended.

flags.quote: Moving your e8-bishop to g6 is a mistake, but taking the pawn on d4 with your c6-knight would be better because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: Nc3 defends d4. Undefended means nobody guards it. Nxd4 is a 2-vs-1 pawn win after recaptures, not a free lunch. You keep using 'undefended' as a synonym for 'SEE likes this capture.'

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your c6-knight is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: I just took it and Nc3 was still sitting there. If it was undefended I would not be trading on d4. Say I win a pawn because it was attacked twice, or I will start ignoring the word undefended.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your queen to f4 leaves your pawn hanging to the black d4-knight. A better move would have been moving your queen to d3.
flags.critique: Which pawn, and why Qd3? Nd4 is a beast hitting e6/c2/e2; Qd3 would look at the knight and the center. 'Leaves your pawn hanging' plus a bare suggested square is template noise.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: h6 hits the knight on g5. That is a kick. Empty reasons, empty because. If a pawn attacks a piece, you do not get to say nothing.

flags.quote: Moving your king to d1 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: The eval drops 387 centipawns and you still say strongest. Matching the engine's top UCI cannot mean 'that's the one' when the bar just fell off. Also: which pawn does a king walk save? If this is stepping off Nxc2+, name the fork. If it walks into Bh5+, do not call it pawn rescue.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g4 is the strongest move because your king is harder to attack.
flags.critique: g4 interposes on the h5–d1 diagonal and hits the bishop. That is block-the-check, not vibes about king safety. You even tagged ignored_threat and then buried it under a phrase-bank king_safer line.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on f7 with your h5-bishop puts it where the white queen and pawn can take and you lose a knight. A better move would have been taking the pawn on e6 with your d4-knight because the pawn was undefended and you take the defender of the white f7-knight.
flags.critique: I took a knight with a bishop; the recapture is of my bishop. 'You lose a knight' is the same SEE-bucket lie as Bxf7+. The game ends because exf7+ forks king and queen — you wait until the next ply to mention the royal fork, after calling this a knight loss. Nxe6 taking the defender is the one clause that actually taught.

suggestions.title: Lead with the check, not a later PV pin
suggestions.detail: Qh4+ was the story of plies 5–8 and 10, and the because-clauses were 'pin the pawn to the rook' / 'likely take a pawn' from likely:true PV events. When the suggested move gives check, or the PV of the played blunder starts with a check, rank check/fork on the immediate ply above later-line pins and captures. A 1200 who just hung Qh4+ does not need a ghost pin on h2.

suggestions.title: Stop calling 2-vs-1 captures undefended
suggestions.detail: wins_material already emits 'the pawn was undefended' when seeCp is about a pawn's value, which is true of Nxd4 with Nc3 still guarding. Gate that sentence on defender count === 0. If SEE wins a pawn against a defender, say the pawn was attacked more times than it was guarded. Fixes plies 23–26 in this game and the hanging/undefended synonym bug everywhere.

suggestions.title: Do not save the piece on the square it fled to
suggestions.detail: saves_piece uses ownedPhrase on the destination, so Bc4 'saves your c4-bishop' and Be8 'saves your e8-bishop.' For retreatedToSafety, label the piece from the from-square or drop the square ('saves your bishop from a6 / from e6'). Destination naming is a tautology a novice will mock out loud.

suggestions.title: Print the hanging piece, not a SEE bucket
suggestions.detail: hangingLossCopy maps ~300cp to 'a knight,' so Bxf7+ and Bxf7 both say you lose a knight while a bishop is the unit that hangs. Prefer the hanging NamedUnit's type; use the material bucket only when the unit type and the SEE disagree by more than a pawn. Wrong piece names make every later tactic suspect.

suggestions.title: Prefer kick, unpin, block-check over saves_piece
suggestions.detail: Nf3 covering h4, Bd7 breaking Bb5, a6 asking the bishop, h6 kicking Ng5, g4 blocking Bh5+, e6 wedging d7 — all lost to saves_piece, king_safer, or empty reasons. If the move answers a specific threat (check, pin, attack on a piece), that reason should outrank generic saves_piece/center_control. Empty because on a 'best' move should be a hard fail in the renderer.

suggestions.title: Do not score opening pawn offers as hangs
suggestions.detail: 2.f4 is attacked by e5 by design. Suppress hanging on a two-square king-pawn thrust in the first few plies, or add a gambit/king-file reason so the copy cannot say 'puts it at risk of attack from the black pawn.' Nf3 as the alternative should be framed as development and covering h4, not as refusing to hang f4.

suggestions.title: Never suggest a better move with no idea
suggestions.detail: d4 vs exd6 and Nge7 vs dxe5 are blunders whose better-move sentence has no because. If suggestedBecause is null, fall back to capture/threat/hanging facts on the suggested move before rendering 'would be better.' A verdict without a chess idea is noise.

suggestions.title: Do not call a 387cp swing the strongest move
suggestions.detail: classifyPlayedMove forces best when UCI matches the engine pick, even if evalLossCp is 387 (Kd1). That override was meant for MultiPV noise, not a collapsed eval bar. Cap it (e.g. only if loss ≤ goodMaxLossCp) or switch the verdict to a holds/still-losing frame so 'That's the one' cannot fire on a king walk that drops four pawns of eval.

whatWorked: Bb5: 'you pin the knight to the king' is the actual idea, in one clause.
Ng5+ alternative e6+: forking the d7-bishop and the king is concrete and true.
Qf3 alternative Nf7: queen-and-rook fork is the right shot even if the hanging-pawn lead is sloppy.
Nf7: fork on queen and rook plus the discovered hit on h6 is the rare line that names two real tactics.
Bh5+: fork of the f7-knight and the king matches the geometry.
Nxe6 as the Bxf7 improvement: undefended e6 plus taking the defender of f7 is the correct conversion plan.
exf7+: pawn forks queen and king on an undefended bishop — the game-winner, taught clearly.
